title: Agile transformation and the agile transformation plan
blurb: Explain what an agile transformation plan is, what it contains, when it is needed and how it relates to the change management approach.
question: Which management product can the agile transformation plan replace when a project needs it?

teach.h: An agile transformation is organizational change
teach.body: An agile transformation is an initiative to adopt agility, or more of it, across an organization. Like any organizational change, it moves the organization from its current state to a target state; organizational change management (OCM) is the means by which that transition happens. PRINCE2 Agile gives the transformation its own guiding document: the agile transformation plan.

The agile transformation plan is a plan that guides an initiative to adopt (more) agility. It holds two kinds of content: high-level goals that align the new target states with organizational strategy, such as the mission and vision, and short-term objectives that guide the practical implementation of those target states. In plain English: where we are heading and why it fits our strategy, plus the next concrete steps to get there.

An agile transformation plan typically spans several projects or initiatives, because enterprise-wide adoption takes more than one project. When an organization first tests and introduces agile through a single pilot project, a separate plan might not yet be needed. In that case PRINCE2 Agile suggests updating the project's change management approach to cover the agile adoption instead.

teach.h: Do we need a separate plan?

teach.body: PRINCE2 recommends a change management approach, which can define the target organizational state for introducing the agile mindset and values and how the business moves from the current state through interim states. In the project initiation workshop, under the management approaches topic, the team can replace the change management approach with the agile transformation plan if needed. So the plan is created during initiation, not in the agile enablement workshop held under directing a project.

teach.h: Change management approach or transformation plan?
Success factors and an output, not a benefit
teach.body: The syllabus names three success factors of agile transformations: agile maturity, psychological safety and agile sustainability. These are also the key metrics for agility, first assessed in starting up or initiating a project through agile maturity assessments. One more point: if a project produces an agile transformation plan, the plan is an output (part of the project product, shown under scope on the project canvas), not a benefit. Benefits are the measurable improvements that follow.

Northvale Building Society plans to move its mortgage, savings and branch projects to agile over two years. In the project initiation workshop for the first of these, project manager Grace Adeyemi and agile coach Ifan Lloyd agree to replace the change management approach with an agile transformation plan. Its high-level goals tie target states to Northvale's vision of a digital-first society; its short-term objectives cover training, coaching and the first two release cycles. Had this been a lone pilot, they would simply have updated the change management approach.

teach.text: The agile transformation plan replaces the change management approach (if needed), not the communication or benefits management approach. It is created in initiation (project initiation workshop), not in the agile enablement workshop. And for a single pilot project it may not be needed at all.

items: Agile transformation plan: guides an initiative to adopt (more) agility.
Contents: high-level goals aligning target states to strategy, plus short-term objectives for implementation.
It typically spans several projects for enterprise-wide adoption.
Single pilot project: the plan may not be needed yet; update the change management approach.
It can replace the change management approach in the project initiation workshop.
Success factors: agile maturity, psychological safety, agile sustainability.

summary: You can now explain that the agile transformation plan guides an initiative to adopt (more) agility, combining strategy-aligned high-level goals with short-term objectives. You can also say when it is needed, that it can replace the change management approach in the project initiation workshop, and name the three success factors of agile transformations.

A.q: What is an agile transformation plan, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: A release map covering several releases and iterations
A plan guiding an initiative to adopt more agility
A record of agile risks scored on six sliders
A team plan for the next iteration's tasks
A.why: The agile transformation plan guides an initiative to adopt (more) agility (2.7.1).

whyNot.0: A release map is the agile form of the project and stage plan.
whyNot.2: Scoring agile risks on six sliders describes the Agilometer.
whyNot.3: The team plan covers the next iteration's tasks for the delivery team.

A.q: Which management product can the agile transformation plan replace if needed?
options: The communication management approach
The benefits management approach
The change management approach
The quality management approach
A.why: In the project initiation workshop, the change management approach can be replaced with the agile transformation plan if needed (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The communication management approach covers means and frequency of communication; it is not replaced by this plan.
whyNot.1: The benefits management approach covers benefits reviews and is kept.
whyNot.3: The quality management approach records quality techniques and agile ways of working; it is not replaced.

A.q: Which best describes the contents of an agile transformation plan?
options: User stories for each team, ordered by value
Tolerances for time and cost on every plan level
Detailed tasks for the delivery team's next iteration
Strategic high-level goals plus short-term objectives
A.why: It contains high-level goals aligning new target states to organizational strategy, and short-term objectives to guide practical implementation (2.7.1).

whyNot.0: Ordered user stories belong in the product backlog.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are set through managing by exception, not in this plan.
whyNot.2: Detailed tasks for an iteration belong in the team plan.

B.q: An organization is testing agile for the first time through a single pilot project. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest about the agile transformation plan?
options: It may not be needed yet; update the change management approach
It must be written first, covering the whole enterprise
It should be recorded inside the benefits management approach
It should be drafted by the board in the agile enablement workshop
B.why: For a single pilot, the plan might not yet be needed, so the change management approach is updated instead (2.7.1).

whyNot.1: An enterprise-wide plan typically spans several projects; for a pilot it may not be needed yet.
whyNot.2: The benefits management approach covers benefits, not the agile adoption.
whyNot.3: The plan is produced in initiation (project initiation workshop), not the agile enablement workshop.

B.q: In which workshop can the change management approach be replaced with the agile transformation plan?
options: The agile enablement workshop
The project canvas workshop
The project initiation workshop
The release planning workshop
B.why: The management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop allows the change management approach to be replaced with the agile transformation plan if needed (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer assessments and agile adoption risks for the board.
whyNot.1: The project canvas workshop defines vision, users, options, benefits, risks, scope, cost and value.
whyNot.3: The release planning workshop updates OKRs and the release map at stage boundaries.

B.q: Which list gives the success factors of agile transformations named in the PRINCE2 Agile syllabus?
options: Collaboration, respect and empowerment
Agile maturity, psychological safety and agile sustainability
Velocity, lead time and burn-down rate
Growth mindset, servant leadership and rich communication
B.why: The syllabus names agile maturity, psychological safety and agile sustainability as success factors of agile transformations (2.7.3 to 2.7.5).

whyNot.0: These are characteristics of the agile mindset (2.6.2).
whyNot.2: These are progress measures, not transformation success factors.
whyNot.3: These are concepts that support agile maturity, not the three success factors themselves.

C.q:
Which two statements about the agile transformation plan are correct?
1. It typically spans several projects to enable enterprise-wide adoption.
2. Producing it counts as a benefit of the project.
3. For a single pilot project it might not yet be needed.
4. It is created in the agile enablement workshop.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
C.why: The plan typically spans several projects (1), and for a single pilot it might not yet be needed (3) (2.7.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the plan is an output, not a measurable improvement.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: it is an output, and it is created in initiation, not the agile enablement workshop.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the plan comes from the project initiation workshop.

C.q: At Ashby Water, agile is being rolled out across several projects. In the project initiation workshop, the project manager proposes replacing the change management approach with an agile transformation plan. Which statement about this is correct?
options: It fits, because the plan can replace that approach there
It does not fit, because the plan belongs to directing a project
It does not fit, because the plan replaces the business case
It fits, because the plan replaces the communication approach
C.why: With adoption across several projects, a plan is appropriate, and the project initiation workshop is where it can replace the change management approach (2.7.1, Table 13.7).

whyNot.1: The plan is produced in initiation; the agile enablement workshop in directing a project reviews Agilometer risks.
whyNot.2: The business case is tailored to the project canvas, not replaced by this plan.
whyNot.3: The plan replaces the change management approach, not the communication management approach.

C.q: A project's main deliverable is an agile transformation plan for its organization. Where should this be shown on the project canvas, and why?
options: Under benefits, because it improves agility
Under major risks, because change may fail
Under costs, because it needs a budget
Under scope, because it is an output
C.why: An agile transformation plan is an output, part of the project product, so it sits under scope; a benefit is a measurable improvement (Glossary, 6.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: A plan is not a measurable improvement; the benefits come later from the change it enables.
whyNot.1: The plan is a deliverable, not an uncertainty, so it is not a risk.
whyNot.2: Its cost is recorded under costs, but the plan itself is a deliverable shown under scope.

reteach.title: A route plan for a long journey
reteach.question: When do you need an agile transformation plan, and what goes in it?

blocks.h: Route plan versus a single trip
blocks.body: For a cross-country move you write a route plan: the destination and why it fits your life (high-level goals tied to strategy), and the next few legs of the drive (short-term objectives). For a single trial trip to the next town, you just adjust today's itinerary. The agile transformation plan is the route plan for several projects; a lone pilot simply updates its change management approach.

blocks.text: A plan is an output, not a benefit. The benefits come from the improved ways of working it leads to.

explain.body: The agile transformation plan guides an initiative to adopt (more) agility: high-level goals aligning target states to strategy, plus short-term objectives for practical implementation (2.7.1).

test.q: What do the high-level goals in an agile transformation plan align the new target states with?
options: The team Definition of Done
Organizational strategy, such as mission and vision
The time and cost tolerances of each stage
The priorities agreed in each team's product backlog
test.why: The plan's high-level goals align new target states to organizational strategy, for example the mission and vision (2.7.1).

whyNot.0: The team DoD sets completion criteria for work items.
whyNot.2: Tolerances are set for managing by exception, not to align transformation goals.
whyNot.3: Backlog priorities guide product work, not the transformation's direction.

explain.body: The plan typically spans several projects or initiatives to enable enterprise-wide adoption. For a single pilot project it might not be needed yet (2.7.1).

test.q: How far does an agile transformation plan typically reach?
options: Across several projects or initiatives
Within one team's next iteration
Within a single management stage of one project
Across one release of one product
test.why: An agile transformation plan typically spans several projects or initiatives for enterprise-wide adoption (2.7.1).

whyNot.1: An iteration is covered by the team plan.
whyNot.2: A stage is covered by the stage plan (release map).
whyNot.3: A release is a level of the release map, not the plan's typical reach.

explain.body: In the project initiation workshop, the change management approach can be replaced with the agile transformation plan if needed (Table 13.7).

test.q: During which process is the agile transformation plan normally produced?
options: Directing a project
Controlling a stage
Initiating a project
Managing product delivery
test.why: It is produced in initiation, through the project initiation workshop's management approaches topic (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Directing a project holds the agile enablement workshop, which reviews agile risks, not this plan.
whyNot.1: Controlling a stage manages day-to-day work in a stage.
whyNot.3: Managing product delivery is the delivery team's process.

explain.body: Agile maturity, psychological safety and agile sustainability are the success factors of agile transformations and the key metrics for agility (2.7.3 to 2.7.6).

test.q: Which is one of the success factors of agile transformations named in the PRINCE2 Agile syllabus?
options: Team velocity
Psychological safety
Story point accuracy
Kanban lead time
test.why: Psychological safety is named alongside agile maturity and agile sustainability (2.7.4).

whyNot.0: Team velocity measures delivery rate, not transformation success.
whyNot.2: Story points are an estimation unit; their accuracy is not a named success factor.
whyNot.3: Lead time is a flow metric used in Kanban, not a transformation success factor.
